### PROCESS LXXVII.
**Tincture of Tartarized Tartar.**

#### APPARATUS.
Take Tartarized Tartar, duly prepared according to Process 75 and dried, then ground into a fine powder. Pour over it in a tall chemical vial the purest alcohol of wine, to a height of four inches above the powder. Then, with the vial closed only by paper, let them boil together as gently as possible in our wooden furnace for the space of twenty-four hours. The alcohol will be of a golden color, floating on top, with an aromatic odor and a penetrating, warm taste. If this is repeated with fresh alcohol in the same manner, a white salt will eventually be left at the bottom. The tinctures are thickened over a gentle fire so that a tenth part remains, concentrated at the bottom.

#### USE.
It serves to demonstrate the part in that salt which is dissolved by alcohol. The tincture itself, when prepared, is aromatic, warming, and consolidates ulcers and wounds. The remaining salt, being simpler than before, shows that salts themselves can be whitened once a tincture is extracted by the help of alcohol.

### PROCESS LXXVIII.
**Dissolution of Regenerated Tartar in Alcohol.**

#### APPARATUS.
Take regenerated tartar, prepared as cleanly as possible and with as much care as can be managed, in a tall, chemical, glass vial. Pour over it six times its volume of the purest alcohol and boil it over a gentle fire in our wooden furnace, as prudently as possible. They will combine with each other, and out of these, a single, uniformly composed substance will be formed, with impurities deposited at the bottom. After they have then settled accurately through quiet standing, let the supernatant and pure liquor flow out by a careful tilting of the vessel. If any saline matter that has not yet dissolved remains, it can be dissolved by the application of fresh alcohol with the same caution and separated from the dregs. Then indeed, let the prepared liquors be concentrated by distillation over a very gentle fire to half their volume; the tincture of this salt will be obtained.

#### USE.
You see in this experiment the bringing together into one of alkali, oily acid, the oil of spirits, and vegetables. Hence, the most active principles of plants are freed from inert earth, yet at the same time they are sufficiently safe and not excessively sharp or dangerous. These, indeed, so joined, seem to constitute even the small Elixir of the Sages, which the masters of the ancient Art recommended for preserving and restoring health. It heals almost all obstructions by flowing through the vessels, <column-break/>
penetrating them, and inciting life with an amiable stimulus: thus it heals through perspiration. In chemistry, it also provides a most effective solvent, by which substances are reduced to their smallest parts, active and with their seminal virtue unimpaired, so that they may be admitted into the inner chambers of the body to restrain and subdue any rebellious matter. Nor is it less praised for the beauty of the effects it produces on external bodily ailments, wounds, ulcers, and tumors. Yet this remedy, so wholesome, is not to be denied to the poor due to its supposed exclusivity: for it can be prepared immediately by mixing potash <note>original: "Cineres clavellatos"</note> with fifteen parts of very sharp vinegar, filtering, and thickening. Thus, without the expense of labor or cost, a suitable preparation can be made and used. Known to the ancients in Rome. Pliny, Book XXIII, in the Preface: The ash of vine-shoots sprinkled with vinegar is drunk for ailments of the spleen.

### PROCESS LXXIX.
**Harvey’s Tincture of Salt of Tartar.**

#### APPARATUS.
I take the alkaline salt, very black, which remained in the glass retort after all the volatile matter was expelled by distillation from tartar at the highest heat of sand (according to Process 55). To this, quickly ground into a powder in a hot iron mortar by a hot pestle and placed into a tall glass vial, I pour the best common spirits of wine so that they float four fingers above it. I boil this in a tall vial in our wooden furnace for twenty hours. A black, thin liquor will be obtained with a bitter, aromatic, and lixivious taste. Let this be poured off pure. Thus, it can be kept safe in a closed vessel for its intended uses under its own title.

#### USE.
Common spirit of wine, consisting of water, acid, and alcohol united, when boiled with the alkali of tartar (which is still oily), makes a gentler and safer lixivium because the alkali is tempered by the acid, oil, and alcohol. From this arises a species of medicine and solvent that is quite noble. When boiled or digested in chemistry with vegetables, it produces good results by beautifully dissolving the simples. In surgery, it is a most noble remedy for purifying, cleansing, drying, and consolidating humid, purulent, putrid, sanious, virulent, and cacoethes <note>term: malignant/ulcerating</note> ulcers, as well as those that are fistulous, sinuous, and consuming the flesh; also for consuming those things that grow excessively due to wild flesh, especially if mixed with a little oil according to art.
